title: Resilience stitching playbook - 90-day cross-team pivot (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose and tone:
This is a working scratchpad for a 90-day cross-team pivot to stabilize emerging regressions in model-serving latency and increase SLO adoption across product teams. This doc intentionally mixes tactical checklists, meeting notes, quick experiments, and a lightweight decision canvas — not a polished playbook. Use it as the source of truth for action items and fast iterations while we land the first-phase experiments.

Background (short):
- In Feb–Mar 2026 we observed a 15% tail-latency increase for short-chat routes during bursts. Root causes were mixed: scheduler backpressure with a new batching heuristic (rbatch-v2), and two product routes enabling synchronous reranking without prefix caching.
- Several feature teams have not adopted our recommended SLO templates; others have SLOs but no runbooks. This increases blast radius when serving anomalies occur.

Primary goals (90 days):
1) Reduce P99 latency for short-chat routes back to baseline (<= baseline + 3ms) under the same traffic profile.
2) Increase SLO adoption: convert 6 feature teams that are SLO-less to at least an SLO + runbook state.
3) Create 3 quick rollback/fallback primitives and document how platform will trigger them automatically during capacity constraints.

Success metrics (how we’ll know we succeeded):
- P99 short-chat latency measured globally during 95th percentile traffic windows drops to target for 7 days running.
- Number of feature teams with SLOs + runbooks increases from current 12 to 18.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) incidents for model-serving regressions improves by 25% measured over the quarter.

Stakeholders and RACI (lightweight):
- Sponsor: Jonah Lee (Head of SRE) — approves tradeoffs and capacity for experiments.
- Lead engineer (runtime scheduling): Miguel Hernandez — owns experiments on batcher heuristics and isolation knobs.
- Product relays (feature teams): Priya Desai (hosted-api product) and three product leads — liaison for route-level SLOs and rollout cadence.
- Observability & alerts: Samantha Wu — owns dashboards, synthetic checks, and signal hygiene.
- Platform/Deployment: Platform-engineering on-call rotation — handles canary/rollback pipelines.

90-day plan (high level weeks):
- Week 0 (planning + kickoff): align owners, freeze candidate experiments, create test harness for short-chat traffic replay.
- Weeks 1–3 (rapid experiments): run isolated experiments (see matrix) on staging -> canary with 5% live traffic. Focus on scheduling/batching and cache gating.
- Weeks 4–6 (expand scope): validate top 1–2 fixes on multiregional canaries, add automated fallback policies for affected routes.
- Weeks 7–10 (SLO adoption sprint): partner with product teams to onboard SLO templates, runbooks, and tabletop drills for two teams.
- Weeks 11–13 (consolidation + handoff): bake final configs into platform presets, document fallback playbook, and handoff to runbook owners.

Experiment matrix (quick reference):
- Exp A: rbatch-v2 parameter tuning (max batch latency threshold from 30ms->20ms). Goal: reduce preemptive batching delays. Risk: throughput drop; monitor QPS and token/sec. Owner: Miguel.
- Exp B: route-level prefix-cache enforcement (toggle on for rerank routes). Goal: remove cold-kv loads causing peaks. Risk: memory pressure; monitor KV cache hit rate and eviction. Owner: Platform eng lead (TBD).
- Exp C: degraded model fallback policy (automatic route switch to quantized-variant q1 when tail-latency exceeds threshold). Goal: graceful degradation. Risk: slight quality regression; monitor eval prompts. Owner: Priya.
- Exp D: temporary rate cap during burst windows (token-rate limiter at route ingress for 30s bursts). Goal: protect shared batchers. Risk: client errors; need client communication. Owner: Product relay.

Instrumentation and observability checklist:
- Synthetic short-chat benchmark running every 5m from 3 regions (EU/US/APAC) — baseline and current. Owner: Samantha.
- P99/P90/P50, token latency, batch size distribution, kv cache hit rate, and batch queuing time on single dashboards. Owner: Observability.
- Correlate model variants serving per-request to lat metrics and quality evals. Linked artifact: ENG-4123.

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync (Tues 10:00 PT) — quick status, blockers, and decisions. Use #ops-resilience Slack channel for async updates.
- Daily stand (only while week 1–3 experiments are live) — 15m for heads of stack.
- Postmortem-lite: for any experiment that increased SLO breaches > 10% over baseline, auto-initiate a 24h blameless deep-dive.

Runbook/Play primitives to create (minimum viable):
- Play 1: Short-chat tail-latency triage (checklist: verify synthetic, validate batcher queue, toggle fallback q1, scale dedicated workers).
- Play 2: Cross-team comms template (customer-facing note, internal incident page, triage owner).
- Play 3: Fast rollback (how to revert rbatch tuning, revert route config, and trigger canary 0% traffic).

Risk register (top 5):
1) Quality regressions from fallback quantized models — mitigation: gated A/B eval + holdback set for high-value prompts.
2) Memory pressure from enabling prefix-cache — mitigation: phased rollout and eviction thresholds.
3) Experiment masking due to noisy traffic — mitigation: synthetic replays + traffic tagging for canaries.
4) Insufficient product buy-in for SLO sprint — mitigation: incentives (support credits, dedicated SE hours).
5) Alert fatigue from new signals — mitigation: triage alerts into severity buckets and tune thresholds early.

Open questions (for the kickoff meeting):
- Which three product routes should be prioritized for SLO onboarding in the first sprint? (Propose: short-chat-realtime, short-chat-rerank, embeddings-batch).
- Can platform commit two additional CI/GPU hours per weekday for canary experiments?
- What minimal QA acceptance criteria do product teams require before fallback to quantized models?

Immediate next actions (first 7 days):
- Aisha: schedule kickoff with Jonah, Miguel, Priya, Samantha (done).
- Miguel: prepare staging replay harness and baseline metrics export (due EOD Week 0+2).
- Samantha: create short-chat synthetic monitors in Grafana and set baseline alert thresholds (due Week 0+3).
- Priya: outreach to product leads and gather route owners + current SLO status (due Week 1).
- Platform: prepare canary pipeline with traffic tagging and a rollback hook (work with release-engineering, due Week 2).

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Could try cheap shadowing: mirror 1% of traffic to quantized variant for shadow evals to estimate quality impact without user exposure.
- Consider a temporary customer-facing advisory if we anticipate any visible regressions during public canary. Draft language: "We are rolling out backend performance improvements to improve latency; you may see short transitive changes in response timing for a small subset of requests."

Appendix: quick runbook template (one paragraph):
- Owner, trigger conditions, first three checks (synthetic pass, batcher queue below threshold, fallback readiness), immediate mitigations (toggle fallback, route rate cap, scale workers), stakeholders to page, and required post-action report.

If you edit this doc: please add a short edit note at the top and tag people in the slack thread. Keep actions atomic and include due dates.

— end of scratchpad —
